Nebraska attorney general co-leads group of states raising concerns over climate-related disclosures

By 10/11 NOW
Published: Aug. 24, 2026 at 11:07 PM EDT|Updated: 7 hours ago
Add Us On GoogleAdd as a preferred source on Google
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:36
Instaread

LINCOLN, Neb. (KOLN) - Nebraska Attorney General Mike Hilgers co-led a group of 16 state attorneys general in raising concerns over several major accounting firms’ push for climate-related disclosures in financial reporting.

The attorneys general sent a letter to the “Big 4” accounting firms: Deloitte, Ernst & Young, KPMG and PricewaterhouseCoopers. The attorneys general claim that the firms stand to financially benefit from the additional reporting.

“The Big 4’s climate commitments force clients to make burdensome climate-related disclosures that drive up the costs of their services and place onerous requirements on farmers and small businesses,” said Attorney General Hilgers. “These costs will ultimately be passed on to consumers, who will be forced to bear the burden of increased prices for food, energy, and other everyday products.”

The attorneys general’s letter addresses concerns that the Big 4’s climate activism may violate state consumer protection laws and of the firm’s lack of disclosure on their climate commitments.

In the letter, the attorneys general say that the Big 4 may have also violated state contractual provisions requiring compliance with state law. They warn that this could result in penalties and termination of the Big 4’s contracts.

Joining Attorney General Hilgers in co-leading Monday’s letter are the attorneys general of Texas, Alaska, and Florida. The letter was also joined by the attorneys general of Alabama, Arkansas, Idaho, Iowa, Mississippi, Montana, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, South Carolina, South Dakota, and West Virginia.
